sources.title: Register for VAT: When to register for VAT
sources.quote: You must register if either: your total taxable turnover for the last 12 months goes over £90,000 (the VAT threshold) you expect your taxable turnover to go over £90,000 in the next 30 days

rules.title: VAT thresholds and rates: Flat Rate Scheme joining limit

sources.title: VAT Flat Rate Scheme: Who can join
sources.quote: You can join the Flat Rate Scheme if: you’re a VAT -registered business you expect your VAT taxable turnover to be £150,000 or less (excluding VAT ) in the next 12 months

rules.title: VAT thresholds and rates: Flat Rate Scheme leaving limit

sources.title: VAT Flat Rate Scheme: If your circumstances change
sources.quote: You must leave the scheme if: you’re no longer eligible to be in it on the anniversary of joining, your turnover in the last 12 months was more than £230,000 (including VAT ) - or you expect it to be in the next 12 months you expect your total income in the next 30 days alone to be more than £230,000 (including VAT )

rules.title: VAT thresholds and rates: Flat rate for a limited cost business

sources.title: VAT Flat Rate Scheme: Work out your flat rate
sources.quote: You’re classed as a ‘limited cost business’ if your goods cost less than either: 2% of your turnover £1,000 a year (if your costs are more than 2%) This means you pay a higher rate of 16.5%.

rules.title: Companies House: director and PSC identity verification
rules.value: Identity verification is a legal requirement for directors and for people with significant control (PSCs). A new director gives the Companies House personal code as part of the appointment filing, or when the company is incorporated. A new PSC gives the personal code when first added to the Companies House register, or within 14 days of being added.
rules.display: Identity verification is a legal requirement for directors and for people with significant control (PSCs). A new director gives the Companies House personal code as part of the appointment filing, or when the company is incorporated. A new PSC gives the personal code when first added to the Companies House register, or within 14 days of being added.

sources.title: Verifying your identity for Companies House
sources.quote: If you become a director, you’ll need to provide it as part of your appointment filing or when you incorporate a company.

sources.title: Verifying your identity for Companies House
sources.quote: If you’re a director or PSC, you’ll need to use your Companies House personal code to connect your verified identity to our records for each role you hold. This is part of the legal requirement to verify your identity for Companies House.

sources.title: Verifying your identity for Companies House
sources.quote: If you become a PSC, you’ll need to provide it when you’re first added to the Companies House register, or within 14 days of being added.

rules.title: VAT: every VAT-registered business
rules.value: All VAT-registered businesses use Making Tax Digital for VAT, whatever their turnover. Your first VAT period starting on or after 1 April 2022 is the first one under the rule.
rules.display: All VAT-registered businesses use Making Tax Digital for VAT, whatever their turnover. Your first VAT period starting on or after 1 April 2022 is the first one under the rule.

sources.title: Making Tax Digital for VAT is coming – are you ready?
sources.quote: Businesses need to have signed up to Making Tax Digital for their first VAT return starting on or after 1 April 2022.

rules.title: Income Tax: qualifying income over £50,000
rules.value: Sole traders and landlords with qualifying income over £50,000 in the 2024 to 2025 tax year use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax.
rules.display: Sole traders and landlords with qualifying income over £50,000 in the 2024 to 2025 tax year use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax.

sources.title: Find out if and when you need to use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax
sources.quote: If your qualifying income is over: £50,000 for the 2024 to 2025 tax year, you should’ve started using Making Tax Digital for Income Tax from 6 April 2026 — you can still sign up or sign up your client, if you have not already done so

sources.title: Find out if and when you need to use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax
sources.quote: You need to use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax if all of the following apply: you’re a sole trader or a landlord registered for Self Assessment you get income from self-employment or property, or both your qualifying income is more than the relevant threshold for the tax year — work out your qualifying income

rules.title: Income Tax: qualifying income over £30,000
rules.value: The rule reaches qualifying income over £30,000 in the 2025 to 2026 tax year.
rules.display: The rule reaches qualifying income over £30,000 in the 2025 to 2026 tax year.

sources.title: Find out if and when you need to use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax
sources.quote: If your qualifying income is over: £50,000 for the 2024 to 2025 tax year, you should’ve started using Making Tax Digital for Income Tax from 6 April 2026 — you can still sign up or sign up your client, if you have not already done so £30,000 for the 2025 to 2026 tax year, you will need to use it from 6 April 2027

rules.title: Income Tax: qualifying income over £20,000
rules.value: The rule reaches qualifying income over £20,000 in the 2026 to 2027 tax year.
rules.display: The rule reaches qualifying income over £20,000 in the 2026 to 2027 tax year.

sources.title: Find out if and when you need to use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax
sources.quote: If your qualifying income is over: £50,000 for the 2024 to 2025 tax year, you should’ve started using Making Tax Digital for Income Tax from 6 April 2026 — you can still sign up or sign up your client, if you have not already done so £30,000 for the 2025 to 2026 tax year, you will need to use it from 6 April 2027 £20,000 for the 2026 to 2027 tax year, you will need to use it from 6 April 2028

rules.title: Companies House: accounts filed by commercial software only
rules.value: From April 2028 every company files its accounts in iXBRL format using commercial software. The Companies House web and paper services close for accounts. Confirmation statements and other filings stay on the web service.
rules.display: From April 2028 every company files its accounts in iXBRL format using commercial software. The Companies House web and paper services close for accounts. Confirmation statements and other filings stay on the web service.

sources.title: Companies House update to accounts filing from April 2028
sources.quote: As announced earlier this year, from April 2028, we will require all UK registered companies to file their accounts in Inline eXtensible Business Reporting Language (iXBRL) format using commercial software.

sources.title: Companies House update to accounts filing from April 2028
sources.quote: From this date, our web and paper-based filing systems will be closed for accounts filings.

sources.title: Companies House update to accounts filing from April 2028
sources.quote: Companies House web filing services will remain available and fully supported for non-accounts filings, including confirmation statements and updates to director details.

rules.title: Income Tax quarterly updates
rules.value: Send an update for each quarter by its deadline. These are the standard update periods.
rules.display: Send an update for each quarter by its deadline. These are the standard update periods. 6 April to 5 July: 7 August. 6 April to 5 October: 7 November. 6 April to 5 January: 7 February. 6 April to 5 April: 7 May, in the following tax year.

sources.title: Use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax - Send quarterly updates - Guidance
sources.quote: 6 April to 5 July 7 August 6 April to 5 October 7 November 6 April to 5 January 7 February 6 April to 5 April 7 May (the following tax year)

rules.title: Income Tax final declaration
rules.value: Submit your tax return by 31 January following the end of the tax year. You can submit it earlier.
rules.display: Submit your tax return by 31 January following the end of the tax year. You can submit it earlier.

sources.title: Use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax - Submit your tax return - Guidance
sources.quote: You must submit your tax return by 31 January after the end of the relevant tax year, but you can submit it earlier.

rules.title: Companies House confirmation statement
rules.value: File at least one confirmation statement every 12 months, even if nothing has changed. You can file early. You do not have to wait for the current review period to end.
rules.display: File at least one confirmation statement every 12 months, even if nothing has changed. You can file early. You do not have to wait for the current review period to end.

sources.title: Running a limited company: your responsibilities: Confirmation statement
sources.quote: You must review your records and file at least one confirmation statement every 12 months.

sources.title: Running a limited company: your responsibilities: Confirmation statement
sources.quote: You do not have to wait until your current review period has ended before filing your confirmation statement.

rules.title: Companies House annual accounts
rules.value: File the annual accounts with Companies House 9 months after the end of the company's financial year. You can file the accounts and the Company Tax Return together or separately.
rules.display: File the annual accounts with Companies House 9 months after the end of the company's financial year. You can file the accounts and the Company Tax Return together or separately.

sources.title: Accounts and tax returns for private limited companies: Overview
sources.quote: File annual accounts with Companies House 9 months after your company’s financial year ends

sources.title: Accounts and tax returns for private limited companies: Overview
sources.quote: You can file with Companies House and HMRC together or separately.

rules.title: Revised accounts at Companies House
rules.value: When the directors revise accounts already filed, they must deliver the revised accounts to Companies House within 28 days of the date of revision.
rules.display: When the directors revise accounts already filed, they must deliver the revised accounts to Companies House within 28 days of the date of revision.

sources.title: The Companies (Revision of Defective Accounts and Reports) Regulations 2008
sources.quote: The directors of the company must, within 28 days of the date of revision, deliver to the registrar— (a) in the case of a revision by replacement, a copy of the revised accounts or (as the case may be) the revised report, together with a copy of the auditor's report on those accounts or (as the case may be) on that report, or (b) in the case of a revision by supplementary note, a copy of that note, together with a copy of the auditor's report on the revised accounts or (as the case may be) on the revised report.

rules.title: Company Tax Return (CT600)
rules.value: File the Company Tax Return with HMRC 12 months after the end of the accounting period it covers. A period of account longer than 12 months, up to 18 months, files as two returns, both due 12 months after the period of account ends.
rules.display: File the Company Tax Return with HMRC 12 months after the end of the accounting period it covers. A period of account longer than 12 months, up to 18 months, files as two returns, both due 12 months after the period of account ends.

sources.title: Company Tax Returns: Overview
sources.quote: The deadline for your tax return is 12 months after the end of the accounting period it covers.

rules.title: Corporation Tax payment
rules.value: Pay Corporation Tax 9 months and 1 day after the end of the accounting period, when taxable profits are up to £1.5 million.
rules.display: Pay Corporation Tax 9 months and 1 day after the end of the accounting period, when taxable profits are up to £1.5 million.

sources.title: Pay your Corporation Tax bill: Overview
sources.quote: You must pay your Corporation Tax 9 months and 1 day after the end of your accounting period.

rules.title: Income Tax: partnerships
rules.value: Partnerships will use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax. HMRC has not yet set the date.
rules.display: Partnerships will use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax. HMRC has not yet set the date.

sources.title: Find out if and when you need to use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax
sources.quote: Partnerships will also need to use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax in the future. We’ll set out the timeline for this at a later date.

rules.title: Companies House: changes to directors
rules.value: Tell Companies House within 14 days of a change to a company's directors or their details, such as an address.
rules.display: Tell Companies House within 14 days of a change to a company's directors or their details, such as an address.

sources.title: Running a limited company: your responsibilities: Company information you must report
sources.quote: You must tell Companies House within 14 days if there are changes to: directors or their personal details, like their address

rules.title: Companies House: changes to people with significant control
rules.value: Tell Companies House within 14 days of a change to a company's people with significant control.
rules.display: Tell Companies House within 14 days of a change to a company's people with significant control.

sources.title: Running a limited company: your responsibilities: Company information you must report
sources.quote: You must tell Companies House within 14 days if there are changes to: ‘people with significant control’

rules.title: Corporation Tax: the longest accounting period
rules.value: An accounting period for Corporation Tax is at most 12 months, so accounts that cover a longer period need two Company Tax Returns.
rules.display: An accounting period for Corporation Tax is at most 12 months, so accounts that cover a longer period need two Company Tax Returns.

sources.title: Accounting periods for Corporation Tax
sources.quote: You must file 2 returns to cover the period of your accounts because your accounting period cannot be longer than 12 months.

rules.title: Making Tax Digital for Income Tax: digital records
rules.value: Under Making Tax Digital for Income Tax, your software creates your digital records.
rules.display: Under Making Tax Digital for Income Tax, your software creates your digital records.

sources.title: Use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax - Create digital records - Guidance
sources.quote: You will need to use your software to create digital records.

rules.title: Making Tax Digital for Income Tax: qualifying income
rules.value: Qualifying income for Making Tax Digital for Income Tax is the amount before expenses (turnover), from the tax return for the previous tax year.
rules.display: Qualifying income for Making Tax Digital for Income Tax is the amount before expenses (turnover), from the tax return for the previous tax year.

sources.title: Work out your qualifying income for Making Tax Digital for Income Tax
sources.quote: This is the amount before expenses (also known as turnover), based on the tax return you submitted in the previous tax year.

rules.title: Self Assessment: the balancing payment
rules.value: The Self Assessment balancing payment is due by midnight on 31 January after the end of the tax year.
rules.display: The Self Assessment balancing payment is due by midnight on 31 January after the end of the tax year.

sources.title: Understand your Self Assessment tax bill: Payments on account
sources.quote: You must make your balancing payment by midnight on 31 January the following year.

rules.title: Self Assessment: payments on account
rules.value: Self Assessment payments on account are due by midnight on 31 January and 31 July.
rules.display: Self Assessment payments on account are due by midnight on 31 January and 31 July.

sources.title: Understand your Self Assessment tax bill: Payments on account
sources.quote: These payments are due by midnight on 31 January and 31 July.

rules.title: VAT: the payment deadline
rules.value: A VAT payment must reach HMRC by the same deadline as the return, even when the deadline falls on a weekend or a bank holiday.
rules.display: A VAT payment must reach HMRC by the same deadline as the return, even when the deadline falls on a weekend or a bank holiday.

sources.title: Sending a VAT Return: When to do a VAT Return
sources.quote: You must submit your return and make sure your payment reaches HMRC on or before the deadline, even if it’s on a weekend or bank holiday.

rules.title: VAT: the late submission penalty
rules.value: At the penalty points threshold, a late VAT return brings a £200 penalty, and each later late return while at the threshold another £200.
rules.display: At the penalty points threshold, a late VAT return brings a £200 penalty, and each later late return while at the threshold another £200.

sources.title: Penalty points and penalties if you submit your VAT Return late
sources.quote: When you reach the threshold, you’ll receive a £200 penalty. You’ll also receive a further £200 penalty for each subsequent late submission while you’re at the threshold.

rules.title: VAT: removing penalty points at the threshold
rules.value: Penalty points are removed once every return in a period of compliance is on time and every outstanding return for the previous 24 months is submitted.
rules.display: Penalty points are removed once every return in a period of compliance is on time and every outstanding return for the previous 24 months is submitted.

sources.title: Remove penalty points you’ve received after submitting your VAT Return late
sources.quote: Accounting period Period of compliance Returns to make Annual 24 months 2 Quarterly 12 months 4 Monthly 6 months 6

sources.title: Remove penalty points you’ve received after submitting your VAT Return late
sources.quote: A: complete a period of compliance, submitting all returns by the deadline. B: submit all outstanding returns for the previous 24 months.

rules.title: VAT: when a penalty point expires
rules.value: A penalty point expires on the last day of the month 24 months after the month of the return's deadline, or 25 months after it when the deadline is the last day of a month.
rules.display: A penalty point expires on the last day of the month 24 months after the month of the return's deadline, or 25 months after it when the deadline is the last day of a month.

sources.title: Remove penalty points you’ve received after submitting your VAT Return late
sources.quote: not the last day of a month — a penalty point expires on the last day of the month, 24 months after this the last day of a month — a penalty point expires on the last day of the month, 25 months after this

rules.title: VAT: penalty points thresholds
rules.value: The penalty points threshold is 2 points for annual returns, 4 for quarterly returns and 5 for monthly returns.
rules.display: The penalty points threshold is 2 points for annual returns, 4 for quarterly returns and 5 for monthly returns.

sources.title: Penalty points and penalties if you submit your VAT Return late
sources.quote: Accounting period Penalty points threshold Annually 2 Quarterly 4 Monthly 5

rules.title: VAT: the return deadline
rules.value: A VAT return is usually due online one calendar month and 7 days after the end of the accounting period.
rules.display: A VAT return is usually due online one calendar month and 7 days after the end of the accounting period.

sources.title: Sending a VAT Return: When to do a VAT Return
sources.quote: The deadline for submitting your return online is usually one calendar month and 7 days after the end of an accounting period.
